_about: Character movement values. The walk and the fall are DECODED from the original's listing (planning step 148, G10);
the capsule is still the Godot project's guess.
The listing is out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt (md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0), cited as bytes a..b and
instruction numbers; arguments are pushed last-first (docs/ethanon-formats.md; briefs 00_order 8.0). The Godot
project's walk_speed 160, acceleration 1400, friction 1800, air_control 0.65, gravity 1200 and max_fall_speed 900 are
GONE: the original has no ramp, no friction of its own, no air control and no terminal velocity.
Where the numbers are used: game/sim/Player.cpp (Steer, WalkOriginal, WalkCarried, AirShare, FallPerTick). Those carry
the original's Box2D units into the port's tick through ScriptClock::SimRatio (clock.json physics_step_s); read the
header of Player.hpp before reading a number here as units a second of the port.
ALSO KNOWN (older, from the compiled script's structure): a virtual pad (ScreenPad, SCREEN_PAD_BUTTON, DIRECTION), a
char_feet.ent ground sensor with begin/end contact callbacks, and 'jumpForth' the only jump identifier - the jump

_source: DECODED. SideScrollerCharacter::SideScrollerCharacter (bytes 152667..153096) ins 13-15: speed = SetV4 1077936128 = 3f.
SideScrollerCharacter::applyForces (bytes 129676..130142):
ins 15-24  elapsedTime = float(min(66, g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime())) - the script's whole milliseconds
(STimeManager::getLastFrameElapsedTime, bytes 7894..7961), 16 at a 60 Hz frame (clock.json);
ins 26-36  speedScale = g_scale.scale(speed) x elapsedTime / GetCurrentPhysicsTimeStepMS (33.33: clock.json physics_step_s);
ins 38-56  dirVec = (moveVec.x x speedScale, linearVel.y) - the velocity SET OUTRIGHT, the pad's -1, 0 or 1 across the
body's vertical velocity, no ramp; no pad held is a velocity of 0 (ScreenPad::getDirection, bytes 149614..149699;
arrowKeysMove, bytes 151039..151281, adds -1 or 1 to dir.x);
ins 58-69  isTouchingGround(entity) false (the feet sensor's numTouches, manageFeet bytes 131341..131709): skips to 85 when it is true;
ins 71-84  dirVec.x = linearVel.x x min(1, GetFPSRate() / 60 x 0.86) - the pad ignored in the air (the 60 is SetV4 1114636288,
ins 86-91  SetLinearVelocity(dirVec) (ETHPhysicsController::SetLinearVelocity multiplies by the global scale, 1.0).
scale(x) is x x GetScreenSize().y / 256 (SGlobalScale::updateScaleFactor, bytes 5592..5699, called with 256 from main and preLoop:
briefs 00_order 8.12a; 480 is only the pre-main constructor value), so a velocity of scale(x) is x x H/256 Box2D metres a second,
and Box2D's metre is 50 of the screen's pixels (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:27, :170-177) - 50 x H/256 pixels, which at H/256 pixels a
level unit is 50 x level units a second, whatever the screen. The port's metre is 50 units (Units.hpp), so `speed` is in the port's
metres a second.
At a 60 Hz frame: 3 x 16 / 33.33 = 1.44 m/s of the original's physics, which its 1/30 s step carries 0.048 m = 2.4 units a frame,
144 units a second (150 x 16 / 16.667). MEASURED: F13's walk, about 400 px/s at 2.8125 px/u = 142 u/s (out/parity/footage/F13.md section 3).
movement._elapsed_cap_ms: applyForces ins 15, PshC4 66: min(66, the script's frame ms). The 66 is twice the 33.33 step; no 60 Hz frame reaches it (16 ms).
_air_decay: applyForces ins 75-79. The factor is min(1, GetFPSRate() / 60 x 0.86), evaluated at the matched 60 Hz: 0.86 (the spec's ruling, step
CK's clock). GetFPSRate is the video's frames counted over a window just over a second long, times that window (GLES2Video.cpp
ComputeFPSRate, :878-889: frameCount x interval, an initial 30 for the first second), so a real 60 Hz device reads about 60-63 and the
factor 0.86-0.90; an emulator at 17 fps reads 17 and the factor 0.24: the air brake depends on the frame rate, as the original's physics step does.

_source: DECODED. The world: Game::preLoop (bytes 112536..114414) ins 416-427, SetGravity(vector2(0, g_scale.scale(10))) - ins 405-414 is
V2_ZERO on a no_gravity level, which is zerog.json's - and ETHPhysicsSimulator::SetGravity multiplies by the global scale, 1.0
(ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:670-675, ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:213-216): 10 m/s^2 of the original's physics, 500 units a second
squared, Box2D's own DEFAULT_GRAVITY (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:26). The body: SideScrollerCharacter::SideScrollerCharacter ins 58-62,
ETHPhysicsController::SetGravityScale(2f) (PshC4 1073741824); dark_mage.ent's own gravityScale is 1.
Box2D adds g x gravityScale x its step to a velocity each step and then moves the body by velocity x step, and the step is the
fixed 1/30 s (clock.json): 20 x 1/30 = 0.667 m/s a frame, so 1.111 units a frame squared, whatever the frame's length. At a 60 Hz
frame that is 4000 units a second squared of wall time (4 x 1000: the physics' second is half a frame's). The one cap is Box2D's b2_maxTranslation,
2 m a step (b2Settings.h:101; b2Island.cpp:286, :484: a step's translation above it scales the whole velocity down to it): 100 screen pixels,
35.6 units at the 720-line emulator the footage is from. A fall from the top of a 256-unit level (23.9 units a step) does not reach it; a body that falls on does,
which is what bounds a hidden, dead player's body, that the layer leaves in the world. Player::Steer applies it per tick (below).
CROSS-CHECK: F13's 1-06 fall (out/parity/program/G10/f13/: the player's bounding box per frame from F13_fall_1-06.mp4). The clip's own cadence is the
reference: its median frame gap is 33.9 ms (29.5 frames a second; the gaps run 18-69 ms; no duplicate frames). Per frame, a fall's growth does not depend on the
frame rate (the physics step is fixed): the decode is 1000 units a second squared x (1/30 s)^2 = 1.111 units a frame squared = 3.125 px at 2.8125 px a unit;
the clip's bottom edge on frames #43-#48 grows 2.75-2.96 px a frame squared (quadratic fit 2.96, 2.92 over #43-#50, endpoint difference 2.75; the edge is
quantised to about 1 px), 88-95 % of the decode's. At the clip's 30 frames a second a fixed and a dynamic step coincide, so this proves nothing between them
(F10, at 17-19 frames a second, carries the time base). The walk-off replayed offline ends 84.9 units along at 24 frames a second, 83.3 at 28 and 80.8 at 30
(the clip's is 84.3-84.6), and the replay's fall at the 24-frame fit runs within 10 units of the clip's through frames #43-#50 (rms 5.3 units over the whole run).
gravity._max_translation: b2_maxTranslation (b2Settings.h:101), in Box2D metres a step; the limit in the port's metres a tick is max_translation_m / reference_px_per_unit (2 / 2.8125 = 0.711 m = 35.6 units): Box2D's metre is 50 screen pixels and the port's 50 units, so the screen's pixels a unit decide it. reference_px_per_unit is 720 / 256, the line count every capture of the original is at (briefs 00_order 8.12a; D6 measured 2.8125); on a taller screen the original's limit is fewer units.

_source: WHY A STANDING PLAYER CREPT (planning step 148's amendment, G10-5). The engine integrates a body's velocity BEFORE it solves its contacts
(PhysicsSystem::Update: position += velocity x dt, then the contacts), and Player::Steer adds a tick of gravity to a grounded player's velocity
(Player.hpp: so a descending lift is followed). A player at rest on a slope therefore sinks FallPerTick x dt = 1.111 units straight down every
tick, and the contact pushes him out along the slope's NORMAL: the two do not cancel along the slope, and what is left is 1.111 x sin 15 degrees =
0.287 units a tick down it, 0.278 of them in x. MEASURED: 1-24's ramp_right, 0.278 units a tick in x (out/parity/program/R3/fix2/idle/, x 242.2 at tick 60 and 142.2 at tick 420: 100 units
in 360 ticks), to the digit. A friction on the body cannot touch it: friction acts on the velocity the solver sees AFTER the move (a first try at
this key, a per-tick friction of 0.9 on every idle tick, left 112.5 of 114.2 units of creep on 1-24 in 420 ticks). Box2D solves first and integrates the solved velocity,
so its body, held by friction (mu_mix >= tan of the slope), neither sinks nor slides.
THE FIX: an idle player on the ground is pressed into it ALONG its normal rather than straight down - velocity (-slope x g, -g), g one tick of
gravity - so the sink is normal to the surface, the push-out undoes it exactly and nothing is left along the slope. The slope is read from three
downward probes, one on the body's centre line and one either side of it (Player::GroundSlope); no three hits on one body in one line (a chamfer's
edge or a round top under the body: a first build with two probes drifted a player standing at a block's chamfered end inward, 2.4 units in 27 ticks),
or a slope past what friction holds, and the player is steered as before.
MEASURED (that the original holds): out/parity/original/levels/1-24_t2.0.png, _t4.5.png and _t8.0.png show the idle player on ramp_right at the same
pixel, where a frictionless body creeps 0.278 units a tick, 114 in 420 (planning step 148, deviation 5). DECODED (what holds it): dark_mage.ent
(reference/extracted/assets/entities, UTF-16) carries friction="0.900000", fixedRotation="1"; the original's Box2D mixes it with the floor's own
by the square root (0.47 on ramp_right's 0.25, 0.42 on a platform's 0.2, 0.6 on block00's 0.4, 0.79 on barrel_bomb's 0.7) and the engine mixes
the same way. The port's statics all carry LevelBuilder::kStaticFriction 1, so `friction` here mixes to sqrt(0.9 x 1) = 0.949: a slope holds up
to atan(0.949) = 43.5 degrees, where the original's ramp lets go past 25 (RECORDED DEVIATIONS 14).
NOT BUILT: the original's friction also carries an idle player along a platform that moves sideways under him; this key does not (the player
is still left behind), because the creep is the only thing G10-5 names and G3 (the movers) is its own step.
hold._probe_offset_px: _guess: the two downward probes of Player::GroundSlope stand this far either side of the body's centre line, 6 units apart: a surface's slope is the difference of the two hits' heights over that.
hold._probe_reach_px: _guess: each probe starts this far above the body's bottom (inside the capsule, clear of a resting overlap) and ends this far below it (the feet sensor reaches 5 below: player.json feet).
hold._probe_line_tol_px: _guess: a third probe stands on the centre line, and the three hits lie on one line to within this many units or the ground under the player is not one plane (a chamfer's edge, a round top, a corner within the span) and the player is steered as before. A flat face or a ramp's is exact to a thousandth of it.

1. DECODED - the SCREEN_PAD_BUTTON enum contains exactly three members:
There is no jump button on the on-screen pad. (tools/asbc, docs/original-gameplay.md)
2. ABSENCE - 'jumpForth' is the only jump-related identifier in the whole binary.
3. OWNER-CONFIRMED (Ivan, 2026-08-05): the original had only move-left and
move-right buttons, plus screen taps to create portals. No jump.
NOW DISABLED. The portal mechanic exists, so the harness no longer needs a jump to
be playable. Kept as data rather than deleted so a debug build can re-enable it,
but it is OFF in normal play and a jump-based level solution proves nothing.
_coyote_note: Deliberately 0. A sweep of the binary for buffer/coyote identifiers returned ZERO
hits, which is real evidence the original has no such forgiveness system. This is
the one value here that is closer to measured than guessed - it is an argument
from absence, so still verify it.
